**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Record the admitted lanes before claiming critic approval**

This note marks four leaves as critic-approved, but the candidate tree contains no lane record for any of them covering the required pre-mortem, blast radius, detection, rollback, stop conditions, reviewer identity, candidate SHA, test invocations/counts, and remaining HOLDs; the implementation comments and aggregate commit message do not provide that candidate-bound evidence. Add the durable lane receipts before recording these leaves as admitted.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Tokenize Rust before matching UI surface syntax**

A non-UI REST crate can evade this gate with equivalent valid Rust containing trivia, such as `use axum :: response :: Html;` followed by `Html ("<html>…")`, or `view ! { ... }`: every exact `contains` check is false, and omitting the doctype removes the only markup fallback. Because axum is already expected in REST crates, the build-graph inventory does not catch this case, so the planning-only UI gate can report green for the prohibited surface; use token-aware or trivia-tolerant matching and add evasive fixtures.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Scan Rust modules outside the package directory**

When a workspace crate compiles a module stored outside its manifest directory via `#[path = "..."] mod ...` or `include!(...)`, `rust_sources_under(crate_root)` never examines that source. A non-UI REST crate can therefore place its HTML/view implementation in a shared file at the workspace root while leaving its build graph unchanged, and this planning-only gate reports green; follow or reject external module/include paths, or scan all tracked Rust sources associated with the workspace.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Ignore non-code occurrences of UI marker strings**

Because this searches the raw file text, markers inside comments and string literals are treated as executable UI. For example, a REST-crate regression test containing an inline `view!` fixture, or documentation explaining why `Html(` must not be used, produces `SmuggledUiSurface` even though the crate exposes no browser surface; tokenize the source and restrict matches to relevant syntax rather than arbitrary text.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Classify `-ui` names before competing layer rules**

When a workspace member named `console-demo-ui` is placed under `crates/platform/` or `crates/contracts/`, the earlier path checks return `Platform` or `Contracts` before this suffix check runs; likewise, `console-demo-adapter-ui` is caught by the earlier adapter-name rule. With an ordinary marker-free Rust source, `check_ui_surfaces` then emits no `PlanningOnlyUiCrate`, allowing the exact planning-only UI member this change claims to forbid. Move the `-ui` classification ahead of all competing path/name classifications and add fixtures for these precedence cases.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Scan embedded markup assets for UI surfaces**

A non-UI REST crate can keep its page in `static/index.html`, load it with `include_str!("../static/index.html")`, and return it through a generic `axum::http::Response` with a `text/html` content type. The Rust source contains none of the configured needles, while this collector ignores every non-`.rs` file, so the build graph and source gate both report green for a browser-visible UI. Include tracked markup/template assets referenced by the crate in this scan and add an embedded-HTML fixture.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bind the ledger to the actual candidate SHA**

The preserved PR history shows that the C ledger commit `9c00e3c2abf0455f13b970c4b6a1a21b063ffb9e` directly parents product tip `2b998800dee33cd6d8da7e568268f8ac42ec44e3`, but this frozen authority record names `6cfec81dd892da87480dbf272ebe62ca929f1c06`, which is not present in the repository. Consequently, consumers cannot resolve this receipt to the admitted code, so replace the stale pre-restack value with the actual immutable product-tip SHA.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Scan gate crates for smuggled UI surfaces**

A workspace member under `ci/gates/` can contain an Axum `Html` handler and evade this check solely because it classifies as `Layer::Gate`. This is not necessarily isolated from production: the layer rules explicitly permit `Layer::App` to depend on `Layer::Gate`, while the checked `scripts/console/route-inventory.mjs` only catches `-ui` names and Leptos-family dependencies, not hand-rolled Axum HTML. Remove this blanket exemption or narrow it so every crate that can enter the app graph is scanned.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bind the privilege check to the trigger function OID**

If `leave_api` ever contains an overloaded `kr_labor_guardrails_guard` or the trigger is rewired to a same-named function in another schema, this unconstrained `fetch_one` may inspect the decoy function while the later trigger query verifies only `p.proname`. The census can therefore pass even when the function identified by `t.tgfoid` has a prohibited EXECUTE grant; resolve the exact zero-argument `regprocedure` or perform the privilege checks directly against the trigger's function OID.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
